walkthrough: Goal: use every side button my pen has (the author's Wacom pen has three: nearest the tip, the middle one, farthest from the tip), give the third one its own action, and bend a soft gradient with a steep curve without it breaking into bands.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library. Actions ends with the Pen section; its Pen buttons row says what the buttons do: Eraser · Eyedropper · Undo. Tap it: the page shows in the panel's place: Back, For the buttons your pen has., then Side button 1, Side button 2 and Side button 3, each with Nothing, Eraser, Eyedropper, Undo, Redo and Switch tool as words in two columns, the one it does in the ink pill (Eraser, Eyedropper, Undo), then the eraser end.

Third button: draw a wave with the pen beside the panel (the panel closes as the pen lands on the canvas). Hovering, press the third side button: the wave goes, one undo; keep it pressed: nothing more; release it.

Change: Actions > Pen buttons, tap Redo under Side button 3: its pill slides to Redo. Hovering, press the third button: the wave comes back, one redo. Back shows Actions, the row says Eraser · Eyedropper · Redo.

Failure and cancel: a button pressed while drawing acts when the pen lifts, so a stroke is never cut in two; with nothing left to undo or redo a press does nothing; a button set to Nothing does nothing. The buttons are a setting, never an undo step.
Reopen: leave and let the system close the app, open it again: the wave is there and Side button 3 still does Redo.

Curves on a soft gradient: add a layer, drop the colour (black) onto the canvas: the new layer is black. Type #FFFFFF in the colour panel's field, choose Soft Brush, widen it with the size slider and draw a stroke across the middle: a soft white band with a long soft edge. Adjustments > Curves, drag the middle of the curve left and up: the curve rises steeply from black and the band's dark soft edge stays a smooth ramp while the hand moves (no bands of four levels). Apply keeps it as one step; undo gives the band back.
Not here: an eraser end that does something else; a pen with more than three side buttons.
